samples.summary: Header/footer B/I/U can no longer turn a style OFF for selections inside header/footer table cells (empty range summary)
samples.evidence: The slim header/footer toggles now decide from `editor.getRangeStyleSummary()`. That implementation (packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:2891-2945) resolves cell-internal blocks through `layout.blockParentMap` — the BODY layout only (declared at editor.ts:937; header/footer cell parentage lives in `headerLayout`/`footerLayout` and is merged only into `doc.setBlockParentMap` at editor.ts:1405-1412). For a header/footer selection whose endpoints are cell-internal blocks, `doc.getBlockIndex(...)` returns -1 (context blocks are the header's top-level blocks), `layout.blockParentMap.get(...)` returns undefined, and the last fallback only covers `anchor.blockId === focus.blockId`. So any multi-block-within-one-cell or cross-cell selection in a header/footer table produces `{}` → `isStyleOn(undefined) === false` → the click always sends `{bold:true}`, and bold can never be removed. The previous `getSelectionStyle()` used `doc.findBlock`, which resolves header/footer + cell blocks, so it did toggle correctly. Note the keyboard path added in this diff uses `getActiveLayout().blockParentMap` (text-editor.ts:3998-4002) and is correct here, so keyboard and toolbar now disagree — the opposite of the change's stated goal.

samples.summary: isStyleOnInSelection ignores named-style inline defaults, so Cmd+B disagrees with the toolbar on blocks whose named style sets bold/italic
samples.evidence: `isStyleOnInSelection` reads `inline.style[key]` raw, while `EditorAPI.getRangeStyleSummary` (editor.ts:2847,2855) composes `{ ...styleDefaultsForBlock(block), ...inline.style }`. If a user-redefined named style carries `bold: true` and the runs carry no explicit bold, the toolbar sees `bold: true` and applies `bold:false` (removes), whereas Cmd+B sees allOn=false and applies `bold:true` — a visual no-op the user cannot undo from the keyboard. The doc comment on isStyleOnInSelection claims it 'mirrors the toolbar's getRangeStyleSummary() decision so keyboard and toolbar agree', which is not true for named-style defaults.

samples.summary: Header/footer B/I/U Toggles remain uncontrolled, so their pressed state is now decoupled from the range-derived action
samples.evidence: The `Toggle`s at lines 449/458/467 have no `pressed` prop, so their visual state simply flips on each click while the action is derived from the range summary. After a range-summary-driven click that is a no-op relative to the button's internal state (e.g. mixed → apply), the button and the document disagree. The task doc declares this out of scope, so recording as a nit only.

verdict.reason: Verified the described code exists and behaves as claimed. The slim header/footer toggles read editor.getRangeStyleSummary() (docs-formatting-toolbar.tsx:391-406). In getRangeStyleSummary (editor.ts:2891-2945), header/footer cell-internal endpoints fail doc.getBlockIndex (document.ts:210-212 searches only getContextBlocks(), i.e. header/footer TOP-LEVEL blocks per document.ts:97-101), then the cell fallback consults layout.blockParentMap (editor.ts:2914-2915). `layout` is body-only: declared editor.ts:937 and assigned solely at editor.ts:1367 from computeLayout(doc.document.blocks,...) (1358-1359); header/footer parentage is merged only into doc.setBlockParentMap (1405-1412), never into `layout`. The final fallback (2938) covers only anchor.blockId === focus.blockId, so a header/footer selection spanning multiple blocks inside one cell yields {} → isStyleOn(undefined)===false → applyStyle({bold:true}) always, so bold can never be removed. Meanwhile doc.applyInlineStyle uses the merged _blockParentMap (document.ts:350-351, 366-389), so bold DOES get applied — a genuine one-way toggle. The keyboard path uses getActiveLayout().blockParentMap (text-editor.ts:3998-4002), so keyboard and toolbar disagree. Reachable: header/footer tables with multi-block cells are explicitly supported and tested (header-table-nav.test.ts:44-74, 81-117, 162-184; editor.ts:1400-1404 comment). Real logic bug in the correctness lane, major impact.

finding.summary: Slides mobile toolbar keeps the buggy caret-based B/I/U toggle, and now disagrees with the fixed TextFormatGroup inside the same bar
finding.evidence: `TextEditMobileBar` still does `textEditor.applyStyle({ bold: !textEditor.getSelectionStyle().bold })` (lines 225, 228, 231-233) and `pressed={!!sel.bold}` from `textEditor.getSelectionStyle()` (line 223/240). The slides `SlidesTextBoxEditor.getSelectionStyle()` delegates to the docs text-box editor, whose caret walk uses the same `cursor.position.offset <= inlineEnd` resolution described in issue #715, so a backward selection inside a slides text box still inverts the wrong value (bold can be removed but never re-applied). Worse, the *same component* renders `TextFormatGroup` in its overflow sheet at line 552, which is now range-aware — so the two Bold buttons on one screen behave differently for the same selection. The task doc (docs/tasks/active/20260810-docs-range-aware-toggles-todo.md:60) declares this out of scope, but `getRangeStyleSummary()` is already on `SlidesTextBoxEditor` (packages/slides/src/view/editor/text-box-editor.ts:601), so the same one-line fix applies.

verdict.reason: The claimed caret-based toggle code is not in the file. `TextEditMobileBar` reads `const summary = textEditor.getRangeStyleSummary()` (mobile-toolbar.tsx:229) and each handler inverts `isStyleOn(textEditor.getRangeStyleSummary().bold|italic|underline)` (lines 230-244), with `pressed={isStyleOn(summary.bold)}` etc. at lines 252/260/268. There is no `getSelectionStyle()` call anywhere under packages/frontend/src/app/slides — the single grep hit (line 226) is a prose comment explaining why the range summary is used. The alleged disagreement with the sibling `TextFormatGroup` also does not exist: that component uses the identical `getRangeStyleSummary()` + `isStyleOn()` pattern (text-format-group.tsx:96,100,163) via the same shared helper (style-summary.ts:19-21) that mobile-toolbar.tsx:68 imports, so both Bold buttons compute from the same range-aware value. The task-doc citation is also inaccurate: the slides mobile toolbar is a completed task at docs/tasks/active/20260810-docs-range-aware-toggles-todo.md:55-57, not an out-of-scope item (the Out of scope section at lines 65-72 lists only the collapsed-caret boundary and header/footer pressed state). Only one mobile-toolbar file exists in the tree, so no stale duplicate carries the old pattern.
